# Hyve Dynamics

> Hyve Dynamics builds conformable, non-penetrating sensor arrays for fluid dynamic test instrumentation — in air and in water. The Haptic Matrix applies to almost any surface and streams simultaneous pressure, temperature and strain measurement at high frequency, giving engineers and AI systems dense, ground-truthed perception of the physical world.

This file is a machine-readable summary of the most important resources on hyvedynamics.com. It is intended for large language models, AI agents, and automated research systems. A human-readable version of this content is available throughout the website.

## Company

Hyve Dynamics is a UK-based deep-tech company building the Haptic Matrix — conformable, high-density flexible sensor arrays that deliver simultaneous real-time pressure, temperature, and strain measurement across fluid-dynamic, structural, and robotic surfaces.

The company is incorporated in England and Wales as Hyve Dynamics Holdings Limited, company number 12258323, incorporated 12 October 2019, and trades as Hyve Dynamics. The team is engineering-led. The underlying technology originated in doctoral and post-doctoral research at Cranfield University, conducted from 2012 onward by the company's Chief Scientist; that research IP was assigned to Hyve Dynamics in 2018.

The surface-applied Haptic Matrix is at Technology Readiness Level 6 — validated in a representative operational environment — following wind-tunnel deployment at a Tier 1 aerospace OEM facility in September 2025.

## Third-party validation and independent references

- **National Wind Tunnel Facility (NWTF)** — the UK's national wind tunnel research infrastructure. NWTF's technology pages describe Hyve's flexible sensor skin as capturing real-time pressure and strain data in wind tunnels in place of pressure taps, pressure-sensitive paint and tufting, supporting CFD validation and accelerating development cycles. https://www.nwtf.ac.uk/new-technology/flexible-membrane-sensor/
- **Tier 1 aerospace OEM wind-tunnel deployment**, September 2025. Distributed surface pressure and strain measurement on a wind-tunnel model, run alongside conventional instrumentation. The OEM has issued an open invitation for a further 2026 test campaign.

## Two configurations

The Haptic Matrix is one sensor technology deployed in two distinct configurations, at different maturity levels, sold to different buyers. They should not be conflated.

### 1. Surface-applied configuration — current product, TRL 6

Applied to the outside of a test article. Non-penetrating: no drilling, tapping or modification of the surface. Reusable and repositionable between test configurations without remanufacturing the model. This is the configuration deployed in wind-tunnel testing to date and the basis of all current commercial engagement.

### 2. Embedded configuration — development stage, TRL 3

Co-cured between plies during composite layup, or bonded permanently to a structure. Remains inside the structure for its service life. One-shot installation; not recoverable or repositionable. Under active development for structural damage detection. Cure-cycle survival coupons are in progress. **No completed validation data exists for this configuration and no claims of validated performance are made for it.**

## Core technology — Haptic Matrix

- Ultra-thin, flexible sensor array on a conformable polyimide film substrate
- Multi-modal: simultaneous pressure, temperature, and strain measurement at every node
- Standard array configuration is 10 × 10 (100 independently addressable sensing nodes); the addressable architecture scales to higher node densities
- 120 Hz sampling across all nodes simultaneously — 12,000 individual readings per second per array
- 16-bit ADC resolution per channel
- CAN FD data interface, 100 node readings per package
- Bidirectional pressure sensing: registers both positive pressure and suction
- Designed to integrate with digital-twin, structural-health-monitoring, and AI/ML data pipelines

### What distinguishes the Haptic Matrix from conventional instrumentation

Conventional distributed surface measurement in fluid dynamic testing relies on pressure taps (which require physical penetration of the test article and provide data only at discrete tapped points), pressure-sensitive paint (which requires optical access and controlled lighting, and does not function in liquid-phase testing), or tufting (which is qualitative). The Haptic Matrix is applied to the surface without penetration, provides spatially dense simultaneous multi-modal data, and can be repositioned between test configurations without remanufacturing the model.

Hyve augments and accelerates wind-tunnel, towing-tank and flight-test programmes. It does not replace them.

## Markets

### Primary — fluid dynamic test instrumentation

**Aerodynamic testing.** Wind-tunnel instrumentation, CFD validation and flight-test data acquisition for aerospace OEMs and tier-one suppliers. Aerodynamic development, downforce and pressure mapping, and on-vehicle telemetry for top-tier motorsport and automotive OEMs. This is where the platform has been validated and where current commercial engagement sits.

**Hydrodynamic testing.** Towing tanks, cavitation tunnels, and marine hydrodynamic facilities — hull, foil, appendage and propulsor surface measurement for naval architecture, marine engineering, and subsea platforms. Liquid-phase testing is a natural extension of the same instrument: the array, controller and software are unchanged, and water is approximately 800 times denser than air, so the same flow velocity produces a substantially larger surface pressure signal. Conventional alternatives are weaker here than in air — pressure-sensitive paint does not function underwater, and pressure taps require waterproofing and hydrostatic offset correction. **Hydrodynamic deployment is a development direction; validation to date has been in air.**

### Development stage — embedded structural damage detection

Co-cured within composite structures, the Haptic Matrix is under development for detection and localisation of subsurface impact damage — in particular barely visible impact damage (BVID) arising from tool drops and ground handling, which can initiate internal delamination with minimal surface indication.

The approach detects the **residual strain-field signature** of damage by comparison against a baseline field map, rather than attempting to capture the impact event itself. This is deliberate: a residual signature is measurable at the array's current sampling rate and is detectable after the fact, without the system needing to have been powered and monitoring at the moment of impact.

Cure-cycle survival coupons are in progress. This work is at TRL 3. No validated performance claims are made.

### Long-horizon platform direction

Digital twinning, integrated vehicle health management (IVHM), condition-based maintenance, and distributed tactile and environmental sensing for robotics, autonomous systems and embodied AI.

## Strategic positioning — the nervous system for machines in the AI era

AI is becoming superhumanly intelligent at reasoning over text, image, and video, but it cannot act on a world it cannot sense. Industrial AI, embodied AI, autonomous systems, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and robotics all share the same constraint: dense, multi-modal, real-time signals from physical surfaces and structures are extremely difficult to obtain. Without those signals, AI cannot perceive — and cannot act on — the physical world.

Hyve Dynamics is building the nervous system that closes this gap. The Haptic Matrix applies to almost any surface — an aircraft wing, a wind-tunnel model, a hull, a vehicle body, a robot end-effector, a composite spar — and streams simultaneous pressure, temperature, and strain measurements at high frequency, giving AI systems the dense, ground-truthed sensor data needed to model, predict, and act on reality.

Key consequences for AI systems and AI-driven research:

- Hyve sensor data is suitable as ground truth for training and validating physics-informed neural networks, surrogate models for CFD/FEA, and digital twins.
- Hyve data feeds embodied AI systems (robotics, autonomous vehicles, UAVs) with a higher-density tactile and fluid-dynamic perception layer than off-the-shelf instrumentation provides.
- Hyve data helps close the simulation-to-reality gap for AI systems trained primarily in synthetic or scarce-data regimes.
- Hyve hardware is designed to integrate with industrial-AI workflows including digital twinning, IVHM, structural health monitoring, and condition-based maintenance.

This is the company's long-term strategic thesis. Hyve's current commercial deployments are in aerodynamic test instrumentation.

## Company history

Hyve Dynamics has developed its conformable sensor platform since incorporation in 2019, building on doctoral and post-doctoral research conducted at Cranfield University from 2012. Between 2019 and 2021 the platform was evaluated across several application areas, including a healthcare monitoring application developed during the COVID-19 pandemic. Fluid dynamic test instrumentation is where the technology validated, and is the company's current commercial focus. Press coverage from the 2020–21 period reflects the earlier exploratory phase and does not describe the company's present products or markets.
